transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-26 11:00 AM PT | Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Marcus Lee (Redwood AE), Lina Patel (Redwood SE), Rohit Menon (Redwood SRE) — Sara Gomez (NovaHealth Head of AI), Tom Fletcher (Infra Lead), Priya Narayan (Security)

Summary: quick weekly sync, benchmark numbers vs BaselineAI, discuss tuning knobs, agree next steps.

[00:00] Marcus Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, Sara, Tom, Priya — can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Sara Gomez: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:07] Tom Fletcher: Good morning. Audio is fine.
[00:10] Marcus Lee: Cool. Quick agenda — we'll run through the benchmark numbers we uploaded yesterday, compare Redwood end-to-end p50/p95 and throughput against the baseline provider, then Lina will talk tuning knobs and Rohit will cover infra notes. We'll leave time for security questions.
[00:28] Lina Patel: Sounds good. I'm going to share my screen, hopefully firefly didn't kill the share... oh wait um okay yes, I can see the spreadsheet. The file is the one Marcus shared: "redwood-vs-baseline-benchmarks-2026-05-25.csv".
[00:45] Marcus Lee: Note — numbers here are from our dedicated POC pool (2x A100 equivalent), synthetic load mimicking your 80/20 short/long prompt mix. BaselineAI numbers are from their managed endpoint using equivalent GPU family per their spec sheet.
[01:05] Lina Patel: First slide/first table — latency summary. Redwood p50 is 110ms, p95 420ms for the 512-token workload. Baseline p50 140ms, p95 520ms. So overall p95 improved ~19% on Redwood in our runs.
[01:28] Tom Fletcher: Hmm, that's promising. How consistent was the baseline test? Did you isolate cold starts?
[01:35] Lina Patel: We warmed both endpoints with a 10-minute ramp, then ran steady-state for 20 minutes per run. We repeated 3 runs; numbers are median across runs. There are some small variance spikes on baseline during simultaneous requests.
[01:50] Rohit Menon: Also worth calling out: our test had prefix/K-V cache enabled — sorry transcription/ops notes, K V cache — which helps for the 80% short prompt reuse; that reduced token compute by about 12%. BaselineAI's endpoint doesn't support equivalent caching in their managed profile per their docs. That helps the p95.
[02:15] Priya Narayan: Can you clarify caching — is any customer PII stored in cache? From security side we need encryption at rest and TTLs and audit logs.
[02:26] Lina Patel: Great question. In the POC we used ephemeral prefix caching in memory on the instance; nothing persisted to disk. By default TTL is 30 minutes for the POC but that is configurable and can be disabled. For private deployment you can plug into KMS and audit logs.
[02:45] Sara Gomez: Ok that's good, we'll follow up on KMS details.
[02:50] Marcus Lee: Back to performance — throughput table: with concurrency of 32 we saw steady-state throughput of 240 QPS for Redwood on that workload, Baseline at 210 QPS. So roughly 14% better throughput in our environment.
[03:12] Tom Fletcher: Did you push to GPU saturation? I want to make sure numbers are realistic at our target 500 QPS.
[03:18] Lina Patel: Not at full saturation; we sized test to reflect current expected POC traffic. We can run a saturation test next week — stress test to find the knee.
[03:27] Sara Gomez: We need the knee. Our production target is p95 under 600ms at 500 QPS -- that's our SLA.
[03:35] Marcus Lee: Yeah that's helpful to know. Action: Tom share exact traffic profile (we asked already) — that'll let us run scaled saturation test.
[03:43] Tom Fletcher: I can pull that and share by EOD Monday.
[03:45] Priya Narayan: Also can you confirm region/placement? Data residency matters.
[03:50] Rohit Menon: For the POC we ran in us-west-2. We can mirror in your preferred region; for Private/VPC we can deploy into your cloud region or an on-prem cluster.
[04:05] Sara Gomez: Good.
[04:07] Lina Patel: I want to call out one more thing — tokenization/sequence length distribution. The 20% long prompts skew p95. We ran a short-only distribution and p95 dropped to 240ms. So workload mix matters a lot.
[04:22] Marcus Lee: Right — that's why we asked for your traffic samples, Tom.
[04:26] Tom Fletcher: I'll anonymize and send.
[04:30] [05:00] Marcus Lee: Turning to tuning — Lina, can you walk through practical levers?
[05:04] Lina Patel: Yeah. Three quick levers we tested: batching, KV/prefix cache, and quantization. Batching — we tested dynamic batching up to 64 and it improved throughput but increased tail latency; the sweet spot for this workload was concurrency 24, batch size ~16. For quantization we tried 4-bit quant on the model and saw a ~25% reduction in memory and ~12% latency improvement but a small quality delta on edge cases; we flagged that in the eval set.
[05:40] Sara Gomez: On quality delta — can you show example failures? We need to know if hallucinations increased.
[05:46] Lina Patel: We have a small eval set in the spreadsheet under the "quality_notes" tab, some examples where answers were slightly shorter or missed a nuance. We don't see systematic hallucinations, but fine-tuning prompts or using the 8-bit path is an option if quality must be preserved.
[06:05] Priya Narayan: Does quantization affect encryption or KMS?
[06:08] Rohit Menon: No — quantization is a runtime representation; encryption/KMS is orthogonal. Key concern is whether model artifacts leave the customer environment. For Redwood Private we can keep artifacts in-customer.
[06:20] Tom Fletcher: For Dedicated vs Hosted — cost delta? BaselineAI quoted a flat per-token + infra premium in their managed plan; Redwood's Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and the quantization option lowers infra. We'll need a cost worksheet.
[06:35] Marcus Lee: We'll include a simple cost comparison in the spreadsheet.
[06:40] [07:00] Sara Gomez: Were there any error cases? Timeouts, retries?
[07:04] Lina Patel: A couple of 503s at very high concurrency on baseline tests. On Redwood we observed transient queuing events during bursts, but retries succeeded; overall error rate <0.1% in our runs.
[07:20] Tom Fletcher: What about KV cache hit rates?
[07:24] Lina Patel: For the 80/20 workload we saw ~34% cache hit rate, translating to roughly 12% CPU/GPU saved and about 10-15% p95 improvement. If you have more reuse patterns hit rate can be higher.
[07:38] Priya Narayan: Audit logs — are they per-request? Need to ensure we can ingest into Splunk.
[07:44] Rohit Menon: Yes, we can emit per-request traces and logs with correlation IDs and you can forward to Splunk/Datadog. In Private we also support longer retention.
[07:58] [08:15] Marcus Lee: Ok let's surface the ask list: tests to run next week — saturation run to find knee, region mirrored test, and a quantization A/B run with eval harness. Lina will prepare tuning configs.
[08:30] Lina Patel: I'll prepare a config repo with example tuning flags: dynamic_batching: true/false, batch_target: 16, prefix_cache_ttl: 0/1800, quant_mode: int4/int8/float16, kernel_selection: auto/manual.
[08:50] Sara Gomez: That looks good. A couple of quick security follow-ups: SOC2 cert — do you have a whitepaper?
[08:58] Marcus Lee: We do — I'll send the SOC2 and ISO docs. For POC we can provide the security pack and a redacted SOC2 report.
[09:07] Priya Narayan: Also SSO/SAML — we need SAML metadata to onboard.
[09:11] Marcus Lee: We'll add SAML metadata and SSO onboarding instructions to the share.
[09:15] Tom Fletcher: One more infra question — did you test autoscaling? If we get bursts during business hours we need fast spin-up.
[09:23] Rohit Menon: POC pool had autoscale on with a pre-warm threshold; observed spin-up time ~18-30s for a new instance to be ready for traffic, depending on region. For Dedicated you can preallocate burst capacity to reduce spin-up.
[09:40] Sara Gomez: 18-30s is fine but we need cold-start numbers for worst-case.
[09:45] Lina Patel: We'll run a cold-start test and send numbers.
[09:50] [10:00] Marcus Lee: Any blockers on your side?
[10:03] Tom Fletcher: Nothing blocker, just need the saturation test and the exact traffic sample.
[10:07] Priya Narayan: Security will review SOC2 and KMS docs; we'll get back with any follow-ups.
[10:12] Sara Gomez: For quality, can you also run the eval harness against quantized model and include diffs?
[10:18] Lina Patel: Yes, we'll include per-example diffs and flag any unacceptable deltas.
[10:23] Marcus Lee: Great. To recap, action items: Marcus share SOC2/ISO + updated spreadsheet and raw logs by Friday (2026-05-29). Lina prepare tuning config and quant A/B plan by 2026-06-01. Rohit run cold-start and autoscale timing and region mirror test by next week. Tom provide traffic sample and p95 SLA target by 2026-06-01. Priya confirm KMS/legal contacts by 2026-06-03.
[10:45] Sara Gomez: Thanks everyone. One note — BaselineAI also pushed a recent model update last week; that could affect numbers so we'll want an apples-to-apples run next week.
[10:58] Marcus Lee: Good call — we'll ensure versions are pinned. Lina, we'll pin model hashes in the run metadata.
[11:05] Lina Patel: Will do.
[11:07] Marcus Lee: Alright, thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar for the saturation run and share the files.
[11:12] Tom Fletcher: Thanks.
[11:13] Priya Narayan: Bye.
[11:14] Sara Gomez: Bye.

References/links mentioned: redwood-vs-baseline-benchmarks-2026-05-25.csv (spreadsheet link shared in chat), SOC2/ISO security pack (link), tuning config repo (to be shared).

Auto-generated topics (possible): latency, throughput, kv cache, quantization, autoscale, security

Action items (from transcript): Marcus to share benchmark spreadsheet + raw logs (due 2026-05-29); Lina to prepare tuning + quant plan (due 2026-06-01); Tom to share traffic sample and p95 SLA (due 2026-06-01); Rohit to run cold-start & autoscale tests (due 2026-06-04); Priya to confirm KMS/legal contacts (due 2026-06-03).

End of transcript.
